No supplied paper specifically mentions or studies “van der Klis Lorentz neural networks” or “Lorentz neural networks” under the specific attribution to van der Klis.

However, paper [1] is a Lorentz (Lorentz-model hyperbolic space) neural network method by Robert van der Klis and coauthors. It argues that existing Lorentz linear layers make hyperbolic norms scale logarithmically with the number of gradient descent steps, and proposes a new distance-to-hyperplane grounded Lorentz linear layer to recover linear scaling while maintaining hyperbolic geometry, with additional efficiency mechanisms via Lorentzian activations and caching.

The other supplied papers are about different architectures (e.g., Clifford algebra networks [2], quadratic-form training [4], nonlinear vector autoregressive models [5], neural operators [6,7], etc.) and do not address Lorentz hyperbolic networks.
